dryEvidence: The security-relevant surface of this change is the bypass-grant trust boundary and the recovery-exception command matcher. Every issue found in this area across rounds 11-17 is fixed and each fix is pinned by a test verified load-bearing (hand-revert the fix, confirm the new test fails, restore, confirm it passes): host-side grant verification so the manifest signing key never crosses into project-resolved code; one-shot atomic grant claim via bare unlinkSync with no existsSync pre-check; TOCTOU-safe grant reads that open once with O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and then fstat/read by fd rather than by path; refusal (not silent persistence) of an oversized grant write; grant-schema bump to v2 so written_at is signed. Round 18 (agy) examined all 44 changed files under this lens and reported 0 findings; Round 19's only finding was a rails violation, not a security defect. On the current revision the mutation gate kills the mutants planted in bypass-grant.mjs, recovery-exception.mjs, mutation-gate.mjs, and both hosts' handoff gates, so these guards are demonstrably load-bearing rather than decorative.

dryEvidence: The two correctness cores are (a) the threshold recalibration — retiring observed.bytes from the band evaluation and replacing MAX_SCAN_BYTES with MAX_ACTIVE_CONTEXT_BYTES plus MAX_SCAN_WALL_MS, reporting an accumulated lower-bound depth instead of +Infinity on budget exhaustion — and (b) authorized() in mutation-gate.mjs, where Round 17 found that a same-session bound grant could not clear the exact unbound marker shape the gate's own producer creates, meaning the recovery mechanism never actually worked for the ordinary lockout case. Both are fixed and pinned. The scan deadline was additionally made genuinely preemptive against blocking I/O by moving the tail read into a spawnSync'd child with a real timeout and SIGKILL, after discovering and fixing a truncation bug where process.exit() after a large stdout write cut the payload at the OS pipe buffer. Round 18 reported 0 correctness findings; Round 19 reported none in this lens. On the current revision, mutants planted at thresholds.mjs:27, mutation-gate.mjs:104, adapter.mjs:88, and paths.mjs:50 are all killed.

dryEvidence: adlc behavior-diff is not applicable to this change: it captures and compares an HTTP surface, and this Phase 0 hotfix changes no HTTP surface — it alters hook-time gate decisions and a local recovery CLI. The observable behavior change is therefore surfaced for the P6 human gate through the gate manifest and the deny-path tests rather than a behavior-diff artifact. The intended behavior delta is precisely: a session whose on-disk transcript exceeds the old 256KiB MAX_SCAN_BYTES no longer receives a +Infinity depth and a false Hard-Degraded lockout; bare `pwd` is always allowed; the operator's own handoff.mjs recovery commands are allowed ahead of any deny check under a grammar-matched, tool-identity-gated, same-session-bound exception; and every deny diagnostic now prints a literal, copy-pasteable, cwd-independent recovery command for the resolved session id. Each of these is pinned by a deny-path test on both hosts, and the corresponding mutants are killed on this revision.
